title: Multi-Cloud Cost Anomaly and Spike Detection

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.19 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.19 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`billing:daily` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Cost Management export, GCP Billing export; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Cost Management export, GCP Billing export
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="billing:daily" (provider=aws OR provider=azure OR provider=gcp)
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.19_multi_cloud_cost_anomaly_19"
| sort -_time
description: Sudden cost spikes across AWS, Azure, or GCP indicate misconfiguration, abuse, or runaway resources. Early detection limits financial impact and supports FinOps review.
value: Detecting multi-cloud cost anomaly and spike detection early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Ingest daily (or hourly) cost by provider and service. Compute rolling mean and standard deviation per provider. Alert when daily cost exceeds 2 standard deviations. Correlate with resource inventory for top contributors.
visualization: Line chart (cost by provider over time), Table (anomalous days), Single value (current day vs baseline).
knownFalsePositives: Cloud billing and cost files often arrive a day or more late, include credits and refunds, and use tags that do not line up with app names, so a spike is not always a real overrun. We narrow alerts to sustained trends and we exclude test or sandbox projects when we can.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Cost Management export, GCP Billing export with the modular input for `billing:daily`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest daily (or hourly) cost by provider and service. Compute rolling mean and standard deviation per provider. Alert when daily cost exceeds 2 standard deviations. Correlate with resource inventory for top contributors.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="billing:daily" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="billing:daily" (provider=aws OR provider=azure OR provider=gcp)
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.19_multi_cloud_cost_anomaly_19"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `billing:daily` in `index=cloud` to detect multi-cloud cost anomaly and spike detection. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_19_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (cost by provider over time), Table (anomalous days), Single value (current day vs baseline)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Cost Management export, GCP Billing export and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of multi-cloud cost anomaly and spike detection so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
